title: Memory is fast only next to a disk seek
body: Rough orders of magnitude every engineer should feel: reading from RAM takes around a hundred nanoseconds, while a mechanical disk seek takes around ten milliseconds, a hundred thousand times longer. Caches exist because that gap never closed. Code that looks identical can differ by orders of magnitude purely by where its bytes live.
source_hint: Dean, 'Numbers Everyone Should Know' (approximate, evergreen ratios)
